ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Distribution matching of a 1-step generator against an auxiliary AR model
PROPOSAL: Initialize a 1-step generator from LlamaGen-L teacher weights, feed it a Gaussian latent vector and read out logits for 256 token positions, with tokens drawn by straight-through Gumbel-softmax. An auxiliary AR model trained on generator samples supplies conditionals at the same positions, and the generator update follows the log-ratio of teacher to auxiliary probabilities. Train on ImageNet at 256 pixels with 3 seeds and report FID, Inception Score, precision and recall on 50000 samples.
CONTROLS: Compare with the released DD1 1-step checkpoint and with a set-prediction sampler using 8 steps. Ablate the number of auxiliary updates per generator update at 1 and 5, and the Gumbel temperature.
COST: 360
PREDICTION: FID should land within 15 percent of the teacher's, ahead of DD1. Training could collapse onto few modes if the auxiliary model lags, which would show as low recall.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adversarial 1-step distillation with a discriminator on teacher features
PROPOSAL: Train a 1-step generator from a Gaussian latent vector against a discriminator that reads intermediate states of a frozen LlamaGen-XL teacher, using teacher forcing on generated token sequences. The loss combines a hinge adversarial term with a feature-matching term. Train on ImageNet at 384 pixels with 8 seeds and report FID, precision and recall on 50000 samples, plus the same metrics at 4 intermediate training stages.
CONTROLS: Compare with the released DD1 1-step checkpoint and a 1-step student trained by plain cross-entropy on teacher samples. Ablate the feature layer used by the discriminator and the strength of the feature-matching term.
COST: 360
PREDICTION: Expect FID near 4.5 with high precision but recall about 10 percent lower than the teacher's. The discriminator could overpower the generator early on, so training may stall.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: 1-step distillation of a 775M teacher on ImageNet against DD1 at matched training
PROPOSAL: Distill the LlamaGen-XL teacher into a 1-step generator using auxiliary-model distribution matching, with a Gaussian latent prior of dimension 1024. Train for 200000 iterations on ImageNet at 256 pixels and compare with DD1 trained for the same number of iterations from the same teacher. Report FID, Inception Score, precision and recall on 50000 samples, and the training speed of both methods.
CONTROLS: Compare with DD1 and with a set-prediction sampler using 10 steps. Ablate the latent dimension at 256 and 1024, and drop the auxiliary model update to test whether it is needed.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: The generator should reach FID about 4.0, below the DD1 1-step value, at the same iteration count. A failure would be mode dropping on rare classes, visible in per-class recall.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Effect of the latent prior on 1-step generators distilled from an AR teacher
PROPOSAL: Distill the LlamaGen-XL teacher into 1-step generators with auxiliary-model distribution matching, varying the prior: Gaussian, uniform and a learned mixture, with dimension 256, 1024 and 4096. Train on ImageNet at 256 pixels with 10 seeds for 100000 iterations and compare priors on FID, Inception Score, precision and recall using 50000 samples, plus the same figures at 4 earlier stages of training for the Gaussian prior.
CONTROLS: Compare with DD1 trained from the same teacher and with a 1-step generator that takes discrete noise tokens. Ablate the entropy strength and the number of auxiliary updates, scoring FID on 10000 samples.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Gaussian and uniform priors should differ by under 0.3 FID, about 5 percent, with the learned mixture ahead on recall. Higher dimensions may yield no gain because the generator ignores some latent directions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Toy test of correlation between positions with a known AR teacher
PROPOSAL: Build an AR teacher over 8 binary positions whose joint law is a mixture of 4 correlated patterns, as in the (0,0) and (1,1) example. Train a 1-step generator from a Gaussian latent vector by matching the teacher's conditionals through an auxiliary AR model, and train a set-prediction sampler that emits all positions together. Measure total variation distance to the exact teacher law with 3 seeds.
CONTROLS: Compare with the set-prediction sampler at 2 and 4 steps and with a generator trained by cross-entropy on teacher samples. Ablate the auxiliary model size at 2 settings.
COST: 90
PREDICTION: The 1-step generator should reach total variation under 0.05 while the 1-step set predictor stays near 0.4. Failure would show as a generator that covers only 2 of the 4 patterns.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Sequence length sweep on a tiny VQ teacher with a distribution matching generator
PROPOSAL: Train a 4M-parameter AR teacher on CIFAR-10 tokens from a VQ codebook of 512 entries, then distill it into a 1-step generator from a Gaussian latent vector using an auxiliary AR model. Build sequences of 16, 64 and 256 tokens by changing the downsampling factor, with 5 seeds, and measure FID against the teacher's own samples on 10000 images, plus the same score at 3 intermediate stages of training.
CONTROLS: Compare with a set-prediction sampler using 4 steps and with a generator trained by cross-entropy on teacher samples. Ablate the auxiliary model size and the latent dimension.
COST: 90
PREDICTION: FID against the teacher should rise slowly with length for the matched generator and faster for the set predictor. The auxiliary model could fail to keep up at 256 tokens, which would raise FID.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Full-scale 1-step distillation of a 1.4B teacher on ImageNet at 384 pixels
PROPOSAL: Distill the LlamaGen-XXL teacher into a 1-step generator using auxiliary-model distribution matching with a Gaussian latent prior, initializing the generator from teacher weights. Train for 400000 iterations on ImageNet at 384 pixels with classifier-free guidance applied on the teacher side only. Report FID, Inception Score, precision and recall on 50000 samples, and class-wise recall on the 100 rarest classes.
CONTROLS: Compare with DD1 trained from the same teacher and with the teacher itself sampled with 576 steps. Ablate the guidance scale at 5 values and the auxiliary update ratio.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: The 1-step generator should come within 10 percent of the teacher's FID and ahead of DD1. Rare classes could fail first, since the auxiliary model sees them least often.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Teacher conditionals precomputed on the training set for 1-step distillation
PROPOSAL: Precompute LlamaGen-L teacher conditionals for 1281167 ImageNet training sequences at 3 temperatures and store them, then train a 1-step generator from a Gaussian latent vector to match them, with an auxiliary AR model for the distribution gap. Train for 400000 iterations at 256 pixels, with 3 seeds, and report FID, Inception Score, precision and recall on 50000 samples, plus recall on the 100 rarest classes.
CONTROLS: Compare with DD1 trained from the same teacher and with a generator that queries the teacher online on its own samples. Ablate the temperature set at 3 and 5 values and the auxiliary update ratio.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: Matching stored dataset conditionals should lag the online variant by a few FID points, since they ignore the generator's own samples. Training could fail to cover rare classes when stored conditionals are sharp.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Matched comparison with DD1 and set prediction on a shared teacher
PROPOSAL: Take the LlamaGen-L teacher and build three students under equal training iterations: a 1-step distribution-matching generator, DD1 with flow matching in the embedding space, and a set-prediction model with 8 steps. Train on ImageNet at 256 pixels for 150000 iterations. Report FID, Inception Score, precision and recall on 50000 samples, and the sampling steps the three students need to reach FID 5.
CONTROLS: Compare against the teacher sampled with full token-by-token decoding and against speculative decoding with a 111M draft model. Ablate the number of steps for the set-prediction model at 4, 8 and 16.
COST: 480
PREDICTION: The distribution-matching student should reach FID 5 with 1 step, where set prediction needs 8 and DD1 stays above it. Equal iterations could favor the simpler method if DD1 needs longer to converge.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Seed spread of 1-step distribution matching measured on LlamaGen-L
PROPOSAL: Train the 1-step distribution-matching generator from the LlamaGen-L teacher with 8 seeds on ImageNet at 256 pixels for 150000 iterations, and train DD1 from the same teacher with 8 seeds. Report FID, Inception Score, precision and recall on 50000 samples per seed, with bootstrap intervals from 1000 resamples, and the same figures at 4 intermediate stages of training.
CONTROLS: Compare against the teacher sampled with full token-by-token decoding and against a set-prediction model with 8 steps. Ablate the number of auxiliary updates and the learning rate.
COST: 480
PREDICTION: The spread of FID between seeds should stay under 0.2 for the new generator, below that of DD1. Results could fail to separate the methods if their gap is smaller than seed noise.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Teacher-weight initialization against random initialization for the 1-step generator
PROPOSAL: Train two 1-step generators from a Gaussian latent vector with auxiliary-model distribution matching against the LlamaGen-B teacher: one initialized from teacher weights with the causal mask removed, and one from random initialization. Train for 60000 iterations on ImageNet at 256 pixels with 3 seeds. Log FID on 10000 samples at 12 intermediate checkpoints and report final FID, Inception Score, precision and recall on 50000 samples.
CONTROLS: Compare against DD1 trained from the same teacher and against a generator whose input latent dimension is 512 instead of 1024. Ablate the auxiliary update ratio and the optimizer warmup length.
COST: 160
PREDICTION: Teacher-weight initialization should reach FID 10 in about a third of the iterations random initialization needs. Removing the causal mask may leave the model with poor attention patterns, the probable weak spot.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Learning-rate schedule study for 1-step distribution matching on a small teacher
PROPOSAL: Train 1-step generators with auxiliary-model distribution matching against the LlamaGen-B teacher under 4 learning-rate schedules: constant, linear decay, cosine and a step schedule. Train for 60000 iterations on ImageNet at 256 pixels with 3 seeds, and report FID, Inception Score, precision and recall on 50000 samples, along with FID on 10000 samples at 12 checkpoints during training.
CONTROLS: Compare against DD1 trained from the same teacher and against a generator with a Gaussian latent of dimension 512. Ablate the auxiliary update ratio and the optimizer.
COST: 160
PREDICTION: The cosine schedules should land within 0.3 FID of one another and ahead of the constant rate. Schedule effects could vanish when seed noise exceeds the differences.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Text-conditional 1-step generation distilled from an AR model on COCO prompts
PROPOSAL: Distill a 775M text-conditional LlamaGen teacher into a 1-step generator that takes a Gaussian latent vector and a CLIP text embedding, using auxiliary-model distribution matching with guidance applied on the teacher side only. Train on 2000000 image-caption pairs at 256 pixels. Evaluate on 30000 COCO prompts with FID, CLIP score, precision and recall, and on 500 prompts with ratings from a learned preference model.
CONTROLS: Compare with the teacher at 256 sampling steps and with a text-conditional DD1 student. Ablate the guidance scale on the teacher side at 3 values and the text embedding, using T5 in place of CLIP.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: CLIP score should stay within 0.01 of the teacher's, with FID within 20 percent. Prompts with rare compositions could fail because the auxiliary model sees little of them.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Teacher size study for 1-step distillation on class-conditional ImageNet
PROPOSAL: Distill LlamaGen teachers of 111M, 343M and 775M parameters into 1-step generators with auxiliary-model distribution matching and a Gaussian latent prior. Train on ImageNet at 256 pixels for 150000 iterations with 3 seeds, and report FID, Inception Score, precision and recall on 50000 samples. Fit the gap to the teacher against teacher size and report its slope. Use the same optimizer and schedule for all sizes, with the generator initialized from teacher weights.
CONTROLS: Compare with DD1 trained from the same teachers and with the teachers sampled at full length. Ablate the auxiliary model size and the latent dimension.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: The gap to the teacher should shrink slowly with teacher size, with a slope near 0.1 FID per doubling. A failure would be a bigger teacher whose generator needs more iterations to converge.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Mode coverage of a 1-step generator measured against a teacher on a class subset
PROPOSAL: Distill the LlamaGen-L teacher into a 1-step generator by auxiliary-model distribution matching, training on a 100-class subset of ImageNet at 256 pixels for 50000 iterations. Measure coverage with precision, recall and a nearest-neighbor class histogram on 25000 samples per method, and compare the histogram with the teacher's by total variation distance.
CONTROLS: Compare with DD1 and with a set-prediction sampler using 8 steps, both trained on the same subset. Ablate the auxiliary update ratio and the Gaussian latent dimension at 512 and 1024.
COST: 200
PREDICTION: Total variation to the teacher's class histogram should stay under 0.02 while DD1 sits near 0.05. Coverage could fail on visually similar classes, where mixing of modes raises the histogram gap.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Coverage evaluation of 1-step generators on all ImageNet classes at several stages
PROPOSAL: Distill the LlamaGen-L teacher into a 1-step generator by auxiliary-model distribution matching on the 1000 ImageNet classes at 256 pixels for 50000 iterations, with 3 seeds. Measure precision, recall, FID and Inception Score on 50000 samples at the final stage and at 4 earlier stages, and compare the class histogram of samples with the teacher's by total variation distance.
CONTROLS: Compare with DD1 and with a set-prediction sampler using 8 steps, trained on the full class set. Ablate the auxiliary update ratio and the latent dimension, scoring FID on 10000 samples.
COST: 200
PREDICTION: Recall should rise during training and reach the teacher's within 0.03, with histogram distance below 0.02. Rare classes may stay under-covered because 50000 iterations give them few updates.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Scaling 1-step distillation to a 3.1B teacher with progressive resolution
PROPOSAL: Distill a 3.1B-parameter LlamaGen teacher into a 1-step generator by auxiliary-model distribution matching, starting at 256 pixels and moving to 512 pixels after 300000 iterations, with the generator initialized from teacher weights. Train on ImageNet and report FID, Inception Score, precision and recall on 50000 samples at both sizes, and compare the quality gap to the teacher with that of DD1.
CONTROLS: Compare with the teacher at full length and with DD1 trained from the same teacher. Ablate the progressive schedule by training at 512 pixels from the start.
COST: 3000
PREDICTION: The gap to the teacher should be under 12 percent of its FID at 512 pixels, against 30 percent for DD1. Training could diverge at the resolution change when auxiliary statistics lag.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Inference speed of 1-step generators measured at several batch sizes
PROPOSAL: Distill the LlamaGen-L teacher into a 1-step generator by auxiliary-model distribution matching on ImageNet at 256 pixels with 3 seeds. Measure sampling latency and throughput at batch sizes 1, 8, 64 and 256 for the teacher, the 1-step generator, DD1 and a 10-step set-prediction model, and report FID, precision and recall on 50000 samples for the generators.
CONTROLS: Compare with speculative decoding using a 111M draft model, and with the teacher at full length. Ablate the key-value cache and the numeric precision used at inference.
COST: 3000
PREDICTION: The 1-step generator should be about 100 times faster than the teacher at batch size 1. Throughput gains could shrink at batch size 256 where the teacher saturates.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Entropy term in the generator loss and sample diversity
PROPOSAL: Train 1-step generators from a Gaussian latent vector against the LlamaGen-L teacher by auxiliary-model distribution matching, with an entropy term on the generator's token distributions at weights 0, 0.01 and 0.1. Train on ImageNet at 256 pixels for 150000 iterations with 3 seeds. Measure diversity with recall, LPIPS between samples from the same class, and FID on 50000 samples.
CONTROLS: Compare with DD1 and with a generator trained by reverse KL alone through straight-through sampling. Ablate the auxiliary update ratio and the temperature of the teacher's conditionals.
COST: 700
PREDICTION: A small entropy weight should raise recall by about 0.04 at a cost of under 0.2 FID. Strong weights could fail by blurring tokens toward uniform choices.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Loss-function comparison for 1-step distillation with matched generator and teacher
PROPOSAL: Train 1-step generators from a Gaussian latent vector against the LlamaGen-L teacher with 4 loss families: reverse KL, forward KL on teacher samples, adversarial and an energy-based score. Train all of them on ImageNet at 256 pixels for 150000 iterations with 3 seeds, and report FID, Inception Score, precision and recall on 50000 samples, plus the same figures at 4 intermediate stages of training.
CONTROLS: Compare with DD1 and with the teacher at full length. Ablate the auxiliary model size and the mix of the loss terms, scoring FID on 10000 samples.
COST: 700
PREDICTION: Reverse KL with an auxiliary model should lead on FID by about 0.5, with forward KL ahead on recall. Adversarial training could fail to converge in some seeds.
